extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys/agents and applicants using ePCT to file PCT international applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural requirements for preparing and filing PCT international applications using WIPO's ePCT system, covering Receiving Office selection, priority claims, names/declarations, documents, signatures, fees, corrections, access rights, and related ePCT features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to choose RO/IB as Receiving Office
rubrics_metrics.description: It depends on the nationality/residence of the applicant(s). See PCT Rule 83.1bis and Rule 90.1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants/agents must check nationality/residence-based eligibility rules (PCT Rule 83.1bis, Rule 90.1) before selecting RO/IB; contact the Receiving Office if unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for RO to transfer filing to the IB
rubrics_metrics.description: Transmittal time depends on the receiving Office's workload; usually done within a few days to one or two weeks; national security checks may delay the transmittal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If concerned about delays, contact the Receiving Office directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing Receiving Office when cloning/changing applications in ePCT
rubrics_metrics.description: When cloning an application, the same RO is retained; however, it's possible to change the RO to RO/IB once (see Change receiving Office).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ePCT retains the original RO on clone operations; use the 'Change receiving Office' function if you need to switch to RO/IB. The system currently only allows changes from other ROs to RO/IB due to validation differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: ePCT policy on allowing RO changes
rubrics_metrics.description: ePCT presently allows changes only from other ROs to the RO/IB because of different validation issues between various ROs and the RO/IB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users are encouraged to use the address book functionality to streamline bibliographic data entry until broader RO-to-RO changes are implemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority period extension for non-working day
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 4C(3) of the Paris Convention: if the last day of the priority period is a non-working day at the authority, the period is extended until the first following working day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to weekends and holidays; consult Article 4C(3) when the 12‑month priority deadline falls on a non-working day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming priority using DAS code in ePCT
rubrics_metrics.description: ePCT uses a real-time lookup to verify the earlier application is in the DAS library; if not registered in DAS, ePCT will not allow selection; use the ePCT Action 'Obtain priority document from DAS' once the earlier application is registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For most DAS-participating Offices the earlier application is registered as soon as the DAS code is provided, but USPTO/EPO provide the DAS code at filing and recording in DAS may lag; follow up with Office of First Filing if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding inventors/applicants after filing (Rule 92bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: You can add inventors or applicants under Rule 92bis. The time limit for submitting such changes is 30 months from the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ePCT Action - Rule 92bis change request if you have access rights, or use Document upload to submit the request; ensure you meet the 30‑month time limit from priority date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor must be an individual (not legal person)
rubrics_metrics.description: A legal entity cannot be an inventor (PCT Receiving Office Guidelines, paragraph 88).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure inventors are natural persons; do not list corporations or other legal entities as inventors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nationality/residence fields: applicants vs inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: Nationality and residence are required for applicant(s) and applicant(s)/inventor(s); for inventor(s) only, nationality and residence are not required and cannot be entered in ePCT; the address (including country) is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if nationality/residence are in the address book, ePCT will not include them for inventor-only entries; IB does not record inventor nationality in RO/101.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking deceased inventors after filing
rubrics_metrics.description: If an inventor is deceased after filing, a request under Rule 92bis should be submitted to the IB; in ePCT, when selecting the inventor you can tick the box 'Deceased'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the online Rule 92bis action (best practice) to inform IB and update records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of Attorney (POA) requirement for filing
rubrics_metrics.description: The IB has waived the requirement for a power of attorney, so it is not needed for filing; however, it may be necessary for certain actions, such as withdrawals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check Official Notices/PCT Gazette/PCT Newsletter and WIPO website for specific Office waivers; when an agent is appointed, a POA may still be required by some authorities for specific actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who can act as agent before a Receiving Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about who can act as agent before the receiving Office with which the application is filed is in the PCT Applicant’s Guide (select the Office and refer to Annex C under 'Who can act as Agent?').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify agent eligibility with the relevant RO in the Applicant's Guide and Annex C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences if the agent is not authorized before RO/IB
rubrics_metrics.description: If the agent is not authorized to file with the IB, the application remains as filed with RO/IB, but the agent will be recorded as the address for correspondence instead of as an agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that lack of authorization affects agent status in records; check where an attorney is authorized to file in the IB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating a new POA signature requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle, the applicant should sign the POA. If authorized by the applicant, the agent may type or copy the applicant's signature (a matter between applicant and agent), which is not checked by RO or IB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practice: obtain an applicant's signed POA; include agent's name, address, telephone/email, applicant details and scope of representation when uploading a custom POA PDF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uploading non‑WIPO-form POA documents
rubrics_metrics.description: You can submit a power of attorney prepared and signed by your client; ensure it includes necessary information (agent’s name/address, applicant details, scope). Model POAs available on WIPO website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model powers of attorney are available in editable PDF on WIPO's site: https://www.wipo.int/pct/en/forms/pa/index.html.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing notification method after filing
rubrics_metrics.description: You can change the notification method after filing; if forms have already been issued they may have been sent using the method selected at filing; updated method applies to future correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Official Notification method - ePCT: Change of Notification Method After Filing for procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default notification setting update planned
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO plans to change the default so that 'Email with links to ePCT' is not selected automatically, allowing users to choose preferred method from the drop-down list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should pick their preferred notification method during filing; if affected by other filing systems (e.g., EPO OLF2.0) coordinate with recipients to ensure access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Troubleshooting preview not showing in ePCT
rubrics_metrics.description: If the preview button does not show the preview file, try different browsers (Chrome, Edge, Firefox), ensure pop‑ups are allowed, and check browser site settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If problem persists, contact PCT eServices Help Desk (pct.eservices@wipo.int or +41-22-338-9523).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings document shown as empty during filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Warnings that drawings seem empty may result from browser pop-up blocking or PDF rendering; whitelist https://pct.wipo.int and https://www3.wipo.int and try clearing cache or different browsers/incognito modes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also ensure the uploaded PDF meets PCT Regulations and Annex F requirements; submit a non-confidential sample PDF to pct.eservices@wipo.int for investigation if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title field formatting best practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Long titles that wrap to multiple lines may be caused by using 'Enter' (new paragraph); use 'Shift+Enter' to create a line break without a new paragraph; filing in DOCX or XML is recommended to avoid issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If title is truncated when converted to PDF, try removing explicit paragraph breaks and use recommended file formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract text extraction precedence
rubrics_metrics.description: If ePCT's automatically detected abstract text does not match the PDF, the IB relies on the PDF document and will correct the extracted abstract to match the PDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you spot a discrepancy, send an ePCT message to the IB after filing to draw attention to it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling formulas/compounds in abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: If compound(s) or formula(e) cannot be properly extracted, tick the ePCT option 'The abstract contains Formula(e)' to inform the IB; the examiner will take them from the specification for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the tick box so the IB knows to pull formula images from the specification when preparing the published abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing ST.26 compliance resources
rubrics_metrics.description: For ST.26 compliance, consult the WIPO Sequence webpage and recorded WIPO Standards webinars for guidance and training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WIPO will forward requests for practical sessions to the team responsible for sequence listing matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Downloading draft copy before filing
rubrics_metrics.description: When the IA is in draft status, you can download a draft copy as PDF or a .zip file for review outside of ePCT; you may also share access rights to the draft with reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share ePCT access rights with the reviewer (e.g., attorney) to allow them to review within ePCT or download drafts for offline review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access by RO and other PCT authorities to filed documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The RO with which you filed can access the application if the RO uses ePCT and has an office account for examination tasks; selected ISA/IPEA also have access if they are chosen in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the 'Office profile' for specific office settings regarding access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting errors after filing: Same day corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: ePCT offers a 'Same day corrections' option allowing submission or replacement of documents on the same day you filed to retain the filing date; other corrections are subject to applicable time limits and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the defect doesn't affect filing date, submit correction within the competent authority's allowed time; missing signature on Request may trigger RO invitation to submit replacement signature sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline for same day corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: The time limit for submitting 'same day corrections' in ePCT is until midnight in the time zone of the Receiving Office; the ePCT cover letter timestamp must show 23:59 or earlier on the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm RO local time zone when filing late in the day if you plan to submit same-day corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of filing fees via ePCT
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing fees should be paid to the Receiving Office. ePCT can only be used to pay fees to RO/IB (see FAQ article: Fees - Online payment to RO/IB).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filing with RO/IB you may pay at time of filing or after filing via ePCT (one month after filing). For other ROs, pay fees directly to that RO using its accepted payment methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paying fees when filing with a national RO (e.g., RO/IN)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you select RO/IN (or another non-RO/IB), online payment through ePCT is not available; fees must be paid directly to the competent receiving Office (RO/IN) using its payment methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the PCT Applicant’s Guide entry for the relevant Office for payment details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees/transmittal when application filed with a non-competent RO
rubrics_metrics.description: If an international application is transmitted from a non-competent RO to the RO/IB under Rule 19.4, the non-competent RO retains a fee equal to the transmittal fee and refunds the remaining fees; the RO/IB will issue RO/102 and applicant must pay fees again to RO/IB including a transmittal fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In total, two transmittal fees may be incurred (one to non-competent RO and one to RO/IB) when transmittal under Rule 19.4 occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signatures when multiple applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application was filed by the applicants, the first applicant with the right to file before the RO (the deemed common representative) can sign the Request form (RO/101). However, generally the signature must be that of the applicant; if there are several applicants, all must sign. If one or more signatures are missing, the RO will not invite the applicant to furnish missing signatures provided at least one applicant has signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Any designated Office may require confirmation by signature of any applicant for the designated State who did not sign the Request, in accordance with its national law. Withdrawals require all applicants to sign. If an agent is appointed, the power of attorney must be signed by all applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted signature formats in ePCT
rubrics_metrics.description: It is possible to sign using a text string signature or by attaching an image signature (.jpg or .tif) in black and white; an autofill function can copy the signatory’s name into the text signature field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you download documents for external signing, remove the signature-field indication before sending; external signature function is designed where the filer is not the signatory (e.g., agents collecting signatures).

rubrics_metrics.name: External signature workflow and visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: When an external signature link is sent, the signatory receives an email with a link to a signing page; the email does not include documents from ePCT, and the signatory cannot view the document on the signing page unless the initiator provides it separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiator should send a copy of the document to the signatory for review by email or other means. The initiator will be notified of approval/refusal and ePCT status will update (e.g., 'signature pending' -> 'signature received').

rubrics_metrics.name: Troubleshooting missing external signature emails
rubrics_metrics.description: If signatories do not receive the external signature email/link, check spam folders and ensure @wipo.int is not blocked by recipient’s email server; if problem persists contact PCT eServices Help Desk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure recipients have valid email addresses and that corporate mail servers do not block WIPO notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: DEMO vs Production mode behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: DEMO mode (https://pctdemo.wipo.int) is only for practicing; a real PCT application must be filed using ePCT Production mode (https://pct.wipo.int). Applications cannot be transferred from DEMO to Production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not file real international applications in DEMO; re-enter in Production when ready to file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account reactivation and strong authentication best practice
rubrics_metrics.description: If locked out after inactivity, reset your password to reactivate. WIPO recommends setting up at least two strong authentication methods to avoid lockout and enable recovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WIPO can assist in removing existing strong authentication after a security check but having multiple methods is more convenient and secure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location and management of Portfolios and Address Book in ePCT
rubrics_metrics.description: Portfolios are created/managed from the Workbench (click arrow next to Workbench). Address Book is accessed by clicking your name after strong authentication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Workbench and Address Book to manage templates, contacts, and streamline filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Template persistence across ePCT updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Templates saved on your Workbench will remain unless someone with eOwner or eEditor access deletes them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Back up critical templates and manage access rights to prevent unintended deletion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting IB/301 and access when filed via third-party systems
rubrics_metrics.description: If you filed via EPO Online Filing 2.0 and did not receive IB/301 or have ePCT access, you can send an ePCT message without strong authentication to request IB/301 to the address for service and then request access rights in ePCT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow up via ePCT messaging to obtain IB/301 and access codes when filing was done outside ePCT production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Granting applicants access rights to manage PCT application in ePCT
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant can be given access rights (eOwner, eEditor or eViewer) by the agent who filed the application using ePCT; the applicant must have a WIPO Account with strong authentication and establish a Connection with the agent’s WIPO Account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once granted eOwner/eEditor access, the applicant can perform actions such as submitting DAS code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating and managing Access Rights Groups
rubrics_metrics.description: To create an access rights group: click your name > Access Rights Group > Add Access Rights Group; you can edit access rights of existing applications including replacing the access rights group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although generic/group emails are possible, WIPO recommends individual email WIPO Accounts for security and traceability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation: use ePCT rather than alternative filing portals
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO strongly recommends using ePCT because it provides automatic access rights, sharing of draft applications, and full ePCT functionality; ePCT-Filing is available with 90 ROs while some other systems (e.g., eOLF2.0/MyEPO) may embed ePCT but not all functionalities are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider training (contacts via pct.eservices@wipo.int) for law firms transitioning from other filing systems to ePCT. Check Office profile for specific ePCT settings and availability.
